content: 1. The World Health Organization (WHO) and the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations published guidelines in 2007 on the safe preparation, storage, and handling of powdered infant formula. These guidelines are accessible online and were last accessed on March 7, 2018. 2. De Marchis, Israel-Ballard, Mansen, and Engmann proposed an integrated approach to human milk banking to enhance newborn care. Their findings were published in the Journal of Perinatology in 2017, volume 37, issue 5, pages 469–474. 3. Bu’Lock, Woolridge, and Baum conducted an ultrasound study in 1990 to examine the development of coordination between sucking, swallowing, and breathing in term and preterm infants. Their research was published in Developmental Medicine & Child Neurology, volume 32, pages 669–678. 4. Woolridge MW discussed challenges in establishing lactation in a 1996 article published in the Food and Nutrition Bulletin, volume 17, issue 4, pages 316–323. 5. A coaching manual titled Improving the Quality of Hospital Care for Mothers and Newborns: Point-of-Care Quality Improvement (POCQI) was made available online and accessed on March 7, 2018. 6. A learner manual titled Improving the Quality of Hospital Care for Mothers and Newborns: Point-of-Care Quality Improvement (POCQI) was published by the WHO Regional Office for South-East Asia in New Delhi in 2017. It was accessed online on March 7, 2018. 7. The Institute for Healthcare Improvement (IHI) provided resources on quality improvement, which were accessed online on March 7, 2018. 8. The Revised Baby-Friendly Hospital Initiative 2018 emphasized breastfeeding promotion and support in maternity care. This initiative included a 20-hour training course for maternity staff, published by WHO and UNICEF in 2009. 9. Baird C highlighted key healthcare stories from 2016, focusing on pay-for-performance models. This information was accessed online on March 7, 2018. 10. Cashin, Chi, Smith, Borowitz, and Thomson edited a publication on the implications of pay-for-performance in healthcare systems, focusing on performance and accountability. This document was accessed online on March 7, 2018. 11. The Breakthrough Series by the Institute for Healthcare Improvement (IHI) outlined a collaborative model for achieving significant improvements in healthcare. This white paper was accessed online on March 7, 2018. 12. The Demographic and Health Surveys (DHS) Program provided a model questionnaire for women, which was accessed online on March 7, 2018. 13. UNICEF, WHO, 1000 Days, and Alive & Thrive collaborated on a report titled Nurturing the Health and Wealth of Nations: The Investment Case for Breastfeeding. This report was accessed online on March 7, 2018. 14. Sinha, Chowdhury, Sankar, Martinez, Teneja, Mazumder, and colleagues conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on interventions to improve breastfeeding outcomes. Their findings were published in Acta Paediatrica in 2015, volume 104, pages 114–134. 15. UNICEF provided additional resources on maternal and child health, which were accessed online on March 7, 2018.
